policies.state_body: North Carolina Utilities Commission; North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality
policies.summary: Any utility or other person building a generating facility whose power will directly or indirectly serve the public needs a certificate of public convenience and necessity from the Utilities Commission, except nonutility clean energy facilities under 2 MW, own-use generators and small leased or community solar under Article 6B. Wind facilities of 1 MW or more also need a Department of Environmental Quality permit, and cities and counties keep their zoning and land use authority over both.
